title: Count and remove a value with Predicate.isEqual

blocks.text: `Predicate.isEqual(target)` tests `Objects.equals(target, t)`: it is null-safe on **both** sides, so `Predicate.isEqual(null)` matches exactly the `null` inputs. Wrapped in `Predicate.not(…)` it matches everything else.
Write two methods in `Matches`; `Predicate.isEqual` is the page's tool for both:

items: `countEqual(List<T> items, T target)` returns how many items equal `target`.
`without(List<T> items, T target)` returns the items that do not equal `target`, in order.

blocks.text: Lists may hold `null`, and `target` itself may be `null`.

cases.says: Occurrences of the target are counted, and without keeps every other item in order.
A null target matches exactly the null items, with no NullPointerException.
Null items are compared safely against a non-null target and never match it.
Items are matched by equals, so an equal value built separately from the target still matches.

concepts: Predicate.isEqual compares with Objects.equals, so it is null-safe on both sides and isEqual(null) matches only null.
